title: Claude Google Workspace Integration Without Code
summary: Claude Google Workspace integration connects Gmail, Docs and Sheets without code. Trigger Claude from Google events and write results back to Workspace.
body_markdown:
## Building a Gmail to Claude to Sheets workflow


You can build this flow in six steps, and each one leaves something that already works, so you never debug more than one new thing at a time.


Before you start, create a Gmail label such as` claude-inbox` and a filter that applies it to the mail you want processed, for example` to:[\[email protected\]](https://www.activepieces.com/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection) -from:me` .


Because the trigger reads the label, the filter decides what Claude sees. The steps below run in order and each ends with what you should be able to confirm.


### Create the trigger and connections


Step 1 is to create a new flow and pick the Gmail "New Email" trigger. Set the label to` claude-inbox` so the trigger ignores the rest of the inbox. What works after: the trigger is saved and scoped to one label.


Now create the connections (step 2). Click Connect in the Gmail step and approve the Google sign-in, then add the Anthropic connection by pasting an API key from your Anthropic Console account.


What works after: both connections show as connected, and you won't be asked again.


Treat the Gmail trigger as a scheduled check rather than an instant push. A message can sit for a while before the flow sees it, so don't test by sending one email and staring at the screen.


### Add the Claude step


Next comes step 3: add the "Ask Claude" action and choose a model. Claude Haiku 5.5 suits high-volume mail like this, and Claude Sonnet 5.5 is the step up if the replies need more judgment.


In the prompt field, insert the trigger's subject and body fields from the mapping panel. Add an instruction such as "Classify this email as billing, bug or other, then summarize it in one sentence."


What works after: the step can read the real email fields instead of fixed text.


Keep the instruction narrow. A prompt that asks for a label plus a sentence gives you clean columns later, while an open-ended prompt gives you paragraphs.


### Write the result to Sheets


For step 4, add the Google Sheets "Insert Row" action, connect your Google account, pick the spreadsheet and tab, and map columns: sender, subject, and Claude's answer.


Put headers in row one first, or the column mapping will have nothing to show. What works after: the flow has a destination and every field has a column.


### Testing and publishing your Claude Workspace workflow


Send yourself an email that matches the filter (step 5), then run Test Step on the trigger and on each action in turn.


Read Claude's raw output before trusting the sheet, because a wrong label here becomes a wrong row there. What works after: you've seen one real email travel from Gmail to a spreadsheet row.


Last, click Publish (step 6). What works after: the flow runs on its own, and the next matching email lands in the sheet without you.


If a later step needs something the connectors lack, a plain HTTP request step covers it. Get this one flow publishing cleanly first.
